questions.q: A software company sets up $m$ number of computer systems to finish an assignment in 17 days. If 4 computer systems crashed on the start of the second day, 4 more computer systems crashed on the start of the third day and so on, then it took 8 more days to finish the assignment. The value of $\mathrm{m}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 17 \mathrm{~m}=\mathrm{m}+(\mathrm{m}-4)+(\mathrm{m}-4 \times 2) \ldots+\ldots(\mathrm{m}-4 \times 24) \\ & 17 \mathrm{~m}=25 \mathrm{~m}-4(1+2 \ldots 24) \\ & 8 \mathrm{~m}=\frac{4 \cdot 24 \cdot 25}{2}=150\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $a, b$ and $c$ be the ${7}^{th}, {11}^{th}$ and ${13}^{th}$ terms respectively of a non-constant A.P.~. If these are also the three consecutive terms of a~G.P.~, then $\dfrac{a}{c}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Let the first terms of A.P.& be $A$ and common difference be $d,$ then

$a = A + 6d$

$b = A + 10d$

$c = A + 12d$

Given $a, b, c$ are~in G. P. $⇒ b^{2} = ac$

$⇒ { \left(A + 10d\right)}^{2} = \left($A + 6d\right)\left(A + 12d\right)$

$⇒ A^{2} + 100d^{2} + 20Ad = A^{2} + 18Ad + 72d^{2}$

$⇒ A = - 14d$

Now \dfrac{a}{c} = \dfrac{A + 6d}{A + 12d} = \dfrac{- 14d + 6d}{- 14d + 12d} = \dfrac{- 8d}{- 2d} =$4$

questions.q: Let ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, \ldots \ldots$. be an A.P. If ${a}_{7} = 3$, the product  \left({a}_{1}{a}_{4}\right)$ is minimum and the sum of its first $n$ terms is zero then $n ! - 4{a}_{n\left(n + 2\right)}$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know the $n^{th}$~term of an A.P. is given by,

${a}_{n} = a + \left(n - 1\right)d$

Given,~${a}_{7} = 3$

$⇒ a + 6d = 3$

$⇒ a = 3 - 6d$

And,~${a}_{1}{a}_{4} = a \left(a + 3d\right)$

$= \left(3 - 6d\right) \left(3 - 3d\right)$

$= 18d^{2} - 27d + 9$

Given product~ \left({a}_{1}{a}_{4}\right)$~is minimum then,

Let~$f ( d ) = 18d^{2} - 27d + 9$

$f^{'} ( d ) = 36d - 27$

Product to be minimum,~$f^{'}\left(d\right) = 0$

$⇒ 36d - 27 = 0$

$⇒ d = $\dfrac{27}{36} = \dfrac{3}{4}

So,~$a = 3 - $\dfrac{9}{2} = \dfrac{- 3}{2}

Given,~${S}_{n} = 0$

${S}_{n} = $\dfrac{n}{2} \left[2a + \left($n - 1\right)d\right] = 0$

$- 3 + \left($n - 1\right)\dfrac{3}{4} =0$

$⇒ n = 5$

Now $n ! - 4{a}_{n ( n + 2 )} = 5 ! - 4{a}_{35}$

$= 120 - 4 \left(a + 34d\right)$

$= 120 - 4 \left(\dfrac{- 3}{2} +$34 $\times \dfrac{3}{4}\right)

$= 120 + 6 - 102 = 24$

$

$

questions.solution:
$S = \left\{x + ka\right\} + \left\{x^{2} + \left(k + 2\right)a\right\} + \left\{x^{3} + \left(k + 4\right)a\right\} + \left\{x^{4} + \left(k + 6\right)a\right\} + \ldots$

$S = \left(x + x^{2} + x^{3} + x^{4} + . . .\right) + \left(ka + \left($k + 2\right)a + \left(k + 4\right)a + \left(k + 6\right)a + \ldots\right)$

$S = x \left(x^{9} - 1\right) \left(x - 1\right) + a \cdot \dfrac{9}{2}\left(2k + \left(8\right)\left(2\right)\right)$

$x \left($x^{9} - 1\right)\left($x - 1\right) + a $\cdot $\dfrac{9}{2}\left(2k + \left($8\right) \left(2\right)\right) = x^{10} - x + 9 $\cdota\left($k + 8\right)\left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)$

So~$45 = 9\left(k + 8\right) ⇒ k = - 3

$

questions.q: Let $x, y > 0$. If $x^{3}y^{2} = {2}^{15}$, then the least value of $3x + 2y$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Using $A . M \ge G . M$, we get

$\dfrac{x + x + x + y + y}{5} \ge x^{3} \cdot {\left(y\right)}^{2}5$

$⇒ \dfrac{3x + 2y}{5} \ge x^{3}y^{2}5$

$⇒ \dfrac{3x + 2y}{5} \ge \left({2}^{15}\right)5 \left(∵ x^{3}y^{2} = {2}^{15}\right)$

$⇒ 3x + 2y \ge 5 \cdot {\left(2\right)}^{15 / 5}$

$⇒ 3x + 2y ⩾ 5 \times {2}^{3}$

$⇒ 3x + 2y ⩾ 40$

$∴$ The minimum value of $3x + 2y$ is $40$

Given $AP$ is $20, 19\dfrac{1}{4}, 18\dfrac{1}{2}, 17\dfrac{3}{4}, . . . , - 129\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Common difference, ${d}_{1} = 19\dfrac{1}{4} - 20 = - \dfrac{3}{4}$

Reversing the $AP$ such that first term becomes the last and last term becomes first.

$⇒ - 129\dfrac{1}{4}, . . . . . . , 19\dfrac{1}{4}, 20$

This is also $AP$.

First term, $a = - 129\dfrac{1}{4}$ and common difference, $d = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

questions.q: Let $a, b$ and $c$ be in~$G . P .$ with common ratio $r,$~where $a \ne 0$ and $0 < r \le \dfrac{1}{2} .$~If $3a, 7b$ and $15c$ are the first three terms of an $A . P . ,$~then the ${4}^{th}$ term of this~$A . P .$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that, the& $n^{th}$~term of a~$G . P .$~with first term~$a$~and common ratio~$r$~is~${t}_{n} = ar^{n - 1} .$

Then,~$b = ar$~and~$c = ar^{2}$

Now,~$3a, 7b$ and $15c$ are in~$A . P .$

$⇒ 14b = 3a + 15c$

$⇒ 14\left(ar\right) = 3a + 15 ( ar^{2} )$

$⇒ 14r = 3 + 15r^{2}$

$⇒ 15r^{2} - 14r + 3 = 0$

$⇒ \left(3r - 1\right)\left(5r - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{1}{3}$~or~$r = \dfrac{3}{5}$

The~only acceptable value is $r = \dfrac{1}{3},$ because~$r \in \left($0, $\dfrac{1}{2}\right]

$∴$~the first term of the~$A . P .$~is~$A = 3a$~and~the common difference~is~$d = 7b - 3a = 7ar - 3a = $\dfrac{7}{3}$a - 3a = - $\dfrac{2}{3}$a$

Also, we know that the~$n^{th}$~term of an~$A . P .$~with first term~$A$~and common difference~$d$~is~${T}_{n} = A + \left($n - 1\right)d$

$∴ {T}_{4} = 3a + \left($4 - 1\right)\left(- \dfrac{2}{3}$a\right) = 3a - 2a = a .$

$e^{\left(\cos^{2}x + \cos^{4}x + \ldots \ldots \infty\right)\ln 2} = {2}^{\cos^{2}x + \cos^{4}x + \ldots \ldots \infty}$

$= = 2\dfrac{\cos^{2}x}{1 - \cos^{2}x} = {2}^{\cot^{2}x}$

$t^{2} - 9t + 8 = 0 ⇒ t = 1, 8$

$⇒ {2}^{\cot^{2}x} = 1, 8 ⇒ \cot^{2}x = 0, 3$

P .$ If the sum of first $20$ terms of an $A . P .$, whose first term is $\dfrac{a + 4b + c}{3}$ and the common difference is $\dfrac{a - 8b + c}{10}$ is $- 444$,~then $abc$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$a^{3}, b^{3}, c^{3}$~be in $A . P .$

So,~$a^{3} + c^{3} = 2b^{3} . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also given~$\log_{\mathrm{a}}b, \log_{\mathrm{c}}a & \log_{\mathrm{b}}c$ are in $G . P .$

So,~\dfrac{logb}{loga} \cdot \dfrac{logc}{logb} = $\left(\dfrac{loga}{logc})2$

$⇒ ( loga{)}^{3} = ( logc{)}^{3} ⇒ a = c$~ ..........(2)

Now from equation \left(1\right) \text{ and } \left($2\right)$~we get,~$a = b = c$

Now,~${T}_{1} = \dfrac{a + 4b + c}{3} =2a$~and~$d = \dfrac{a - 8b + c}{10} = \dfrac{- 6a}{10} = \dfrac{- 3}{5}a$

$∴ {S}_{20} = \dfrac{20}{2} \left[$4a + 19 \left(- $\dfrac{3}{5}$a\right)\right]$

$⇒ {S}_{20} = 10 \left[\dfrac{20a - 57a}{5}]$

$⇒ {S}_{20} = - 74a$

$⇒ - 444 = - 74a ⇒ a = 6$

Hence,~$abc = {6}^{3} = 216$

$

questions.q:
If 19 th term of a non-zero A.P. is zero, then its (49th term):

questions.solution:
Let first term and common difference of $A P$ be a and d respectively, then

$\therefore \quad t_{19}=a+18 d=0$

$\therefore \quad \frac{t_{49}}{t_{29}}=\frac{a+48 d}{a+28 d}$

$=\frac{-18 d+48 d}{-18 d+28 d}=\frac{30 d}{10 d}=3$

$t_{49}: t_{29}=3: 1$

Then the sum of the first $21$~terms of an $AP$, whose first term is $10ar, n^{th}$~term is ${a}_{n}$~and the common difference is $10{ar}^{2}$, is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
For the infinite G.P.&

${S}_{∞} = \dfrac{a}{1 - r} = 5$

Also~$a + ar + ar^{2} + ar^{3} + ar^{4} = 5$

$⇒ a\left(\dfrac{1 - r^{5}}{1 - r}\right) = \dfrac{98}{25}$

i.e.~$1 - r^{5} = \dfrac{98}{125} ⇒ r^{5} = \dfrac{33}{53} ⇒ r = \left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\dfrac{3}{5}$

Now~${S}_{21} = \dfrac{21}{2} \left[20ar + \left($21 - 1\right)10ar^{2}\right]$

$= 21 \left[10ar + 100ar^{2}\right]$

$= 21 \cdot {a}_{11}$

$

questions.q: If the arithmetic mean and the geometric mean of the $p^{th}$ and $q^{th}$ terms of the sequence $- 16, 8, - 4, 2, \ldots$~satisfy the equation $4x^{2} - 9x + 5 = 0$, then $p + q$ is equal to _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& ${t}_{p} \text{ and } {t}_{q}$~is the~$p^{th} \text{ and } q^{th}$terms of the series~$- 16, 8, - 4, 2, . . .$

Here~$a = - 16, r = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Then,~${t}_{p} = - 16\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)p - 1$

${t}_{q} = - 16\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)q - 1$

The roots of the given quadratic equation $4x^{2} - 9x + 5 = 0$~is~$x = 1, \dfrac{5}{4} .$

$AM = \dfrac{5}{4}, GM = 1 \left(∵ AM ≥ GM\right)$

Now, given \dfrac{5}{4} = \dfrac{{t}_{p} + {t}_{q}}{2},$1 = {t}_{p}{t}_{q}$

So,~$1 = $256 \left(- $\dfrac{1}{2}\right)p + q - 2 ⇒ {2}^{p + q - 2} = \left(-$1\right)p + q - 2{2}^{8}$

$⇒ {2}^{p + q - 10} = \left(-$1\right)p + q - 2$

It is equal when~${2}^{p + q - 10} = 1 = \left(-$1\right)p + q - 2$

Hence,~$p + q - 10 = 0 ⇒ p + q = 10$

$
